https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/16/leng.text: Menü Kereső Egy túlélő szerint másodpercek alatt történt a lengyel buszbaleset az M3-ason Belföld Nagy Nikoletta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Éjszaka történt a baleset, amikor a legtöbben aludtak a buszon. Beszéltem az egyik emberrel, aki a buszon utazott. Azt mondta, másodpercek alatt történt az egész. Most kórházban van, nagyon jó ellátást kapnak, a szolgálatok gondoskodnak róluk” – mondta Wojciech Tatara, Siedliska falu elöljárója a Polsat News riporterének az M3-ason történt lengyel turistabusz balesetével kapcsolatban. „Az az ember, akivel beszéltem, valószínűleg még nem hagyhatja el egyhamar a kórházat. Sajnos azt is megerősítette nekem, hogy a településünkről biztosan négy ember meghalt” – mondta az elöljáró. A lap azt írja: nem mindenki tudott még kapcsolatba lépni a családjával, néhányan például kórházba kerülhettek, és nem volt náluk telefon, ezért a hozzátartozók folyamatosan próbálják elérni őket. Lengyelország budapesti nagykövetsége egyébként forródrótot hozott létre a baleset halálos áldozatainak és sérültjeinek hozzátartozói számára. Egy zarándoklat résztvevői utaztak hazafelé azon a lengyel turistabuszon, ami egyelőre tisztázatlan okból letért az útról és árokba borult az M3-as autópályán vasárnap éjjel 1 órakor, a rendőrség hivatalos tájékoztatása szerint a balesetben tizenketten meghaltak . A busz utasai lengyel állampolgárok voltak. Maciej Wewiór külügyi szóvivő azt mondta, hét sérült állapota „nagyon súlyos”, további mintegy 40 személy könnyebb sérüléseket szenvedett. A kelet-lengyelországi Rzeszówban működő Kárpátvajdasági hivatal szóvivője a Gazeta Wyborcza szerint azt mondta, vajdaságból indult zarándoklat résztvevői hazafelé tartottak Bosznia-Hercegovinából. A Polskie Radio Rzeszów szerint a Krosnói Kerületi Ügyészség nyomozást indított a buszbaleset ügyében. Az ügyészség szóvivője, Marta Kolendowska-Matejczuk a rádiónak azt mondta, hogy a lengyel igazságszolgáltatás együttműködik a magyar hatóságokkal. „Az ügyészek és a rendőrök már megkezdték a szükséges eljárásokat Lengyelországban. Tervezzük, hogy egy lengyel ügyész részvételével a baleset helyszínén is vizsgálatot folytatunk. Ehhez várjuk Magyarország engedélyét” – áll a közleményben. Siedliska elöljárója azt is mondta, hogy gyerekek is voltak a baleset sérültjei között, de ők nem szenvedtek súlyos sérüléseket. Wojciech Tatara az egyik érintett gyermek édesapjával is beszélt. „A férfinak maradnia kell, a feleségét talán hamarabb kiengedhetik. Ő a feleségével és a gyerekeivel együtt utazott. A gyerekeknek nem esett bajuk, és az alapján, amit mondott, a felesége is nagyjából rendben van. Neki viszont olyan problémái vannak, hogy valószínűleg nem engedik ki, sajnos ott kell maradnia” – mondta. A Radio ZET egy olyan férfit is elért, aki az utolsó pillanatban mondta le a medjugorjei zarándokutat, így végül nem szállt fel arra a buszra, ami balesetet szenvedett. Wiesław családi okok miatt nem indult el, de több ismerőse ott volt a buszon, írja a hvg.hu . Az egyik áldozat férje felhívta a baleset után, és közölte vele, hogy a felesége, aki Wiesław, meghalt. A buszon 57 utas és a két sofőr utazott. Mindkét sofőr életben van, az Országos Mentőszolgálat a Telexnek megerősítette, hogy vizsgálat céljából őket is kórházba szállították. A rendőrség jelenlegi adatai szerint a sofőr feltehetően elaludt. A Police.hu azt írta: a busz sofőrjét őrizetbe veszik. A tűzoltók éjszaka csörlőzéssel és darukkal emelték meg a buszt , hogy ki tudják menekíteni a jármű alá szorult utasokat. A sérülteket helyszíni ellátás után a miskolci, debreceni, nyíregyházi és egri kórházakba szállítottak. További részletek ebben a cikkünkben . Photograph: Indonesian Geological Agency/EPA Air transport Volcanic eruption halts flights at Jakarta and seven other Indonesian airports Ash cloud from Anak Krakatau affects hundreds of flights and some school and fishing activities Guardian staff and agencies Sun 6 Sep 2026 10.51 EDT First published on Sun 6 Sep 2026 00.29 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Indonesia halted operations at eight airports on Sunday, including from its main international hub, affecting hundreds of flights as a result of an ash cloud from the Anak Krakatau volcano. Saturday’s eruption, which produced lava and booming sounds that were heard up to 435 miles (700km) away, according to Indonesia’s geology agency, also interrupted some school activities and fishing. Two more eruptions were recorded on Sunday. Ash was detected in the airspace around Soekarno-Hatta international airport near Jakarta, prompting authorities to suspend operations. They announced several extensions of the shutdown, keeping the airport closed to flights until 9.30pm local time on Sunday. The suspension affected hundreds of flights, including international ones, according to the airport operator, Angkasa Pura. Singapore Airlines said it had cancelled flights to and from Jakarta for the rest of Sunday. Map The Australian flag carrier said there were “disruptions to a number of Qantas services, including cancellations to and from Jakarta today”. “Our meteorologists and operations teams are closely monitoring conditions in and around Jakarta and any impact on our operations,” it said in a statement. “Safety remains our highest priority. We have contacted affected customers and are providing assistance. Services will resume when conditions allow.” Volcanic ash can damage jet engines, baking on to hot internal parts and quickly wearing out turbine blades, as well as clogging fuel and air systems. It can also damage pilots’ windscreens. View image in fullscreen Passengers wait in the check-in lounge at Soekarno-Hatta international airport. Photograph: Faisal Ramadhan/EPA Ash ‌reached as high as 6,000 metres (20,000ft) ‌on the Java side of the volcano and 15,000 metres on the Sumatra side and some parts of Banten province in Java, the meteorological agency BMKG said. Several ​schools cancelled activities on Saturday after students and residents ​suffered eye irritation, and fishers cancelled fishing trips, the local media outlet Kompas reported. The disaster mitigation agency BNPB said it would conduct a weather modification operation, which could ​include cloud-seeding to promote rain. El Niño-fuelled wildfires destroy precious Indonesian forests – in pictures Read more “If it rains heavily enough, the volcanic ash that has been disrupting our daily lives since yesterday and continuing today will be washed away quickly,” the BNPB chief, Lt Gen Suharyanto, told a press conference. More than 22,000 passengers and 209 flights were affected, the transport ministry said, particularly those bound to and from Singapore. Other affected international routes included Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur. At least 16 domestic flights to Bali were cancelled, local airport authorities said. Anak Krakatau, which means “child of Krakatau”, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra. The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau. That was one of the deadliest and most destructive volcanic eruptions in human history. About 35,000 people were killed. Port authorities said ships passing through the strait were prohibited from going within a two-mile radius of the volcano and should be vigilant. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters Foreign policy UK commits £100m to bolster Ukraine’s air defences over winter Package of military equipment includes Patriot missiles, supplies of which have dwindled amid Russian attacks Jamie Grierson Tue 8 Sep 2026 03.24 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 03.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The UK has committed £100m to boost Ukraine’s air defences over winter with a package of military equipment including Patriot missiles. Defence interceptors, large-calibre artillery rounds and drones will be supplied to Ukraine through the contribution to Nato’s prioritised Ukraine requirements list. Supplies of Patriot missiles, which are used to stop aircraft, cruise missiles, and tactical ballistic missiles, have dwindled in Ukraine, causing a drop in interceptions of Russian attacks , according to military experts. The UK defence secretary, Wes Streeting , is due to co-chair his first meeting of the Ukraine defence contact group, made up of about 50 nations providing military equipment to Kyiv, with his German counterpart, Boris Pistorius, on Tuesday. The UK recently agreed to declassify blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French-produced version of the Storm Shadow, which has already been used to hit targets in Russia. Streeting said: “Both the prime minister and I heard loud and clear on our first visits to Kyiv the importance of supporting Ukraine through this winter, as Putin prepares to use winter as a weapon by continuing barbaric attacks against civilian and energy targets. “We promised to mobilise allies and provide more support wherever we can. Today, we are delivering on that, strengthening Ukraine’s defences and, alongside 50 allies, converting commitment into capability. “We will stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine until they win. Ukraine’s frontline is the frontline for freedom everywhere and our support will not waver.” The prime minister, Andy Burnham, spoke to the US president, Donald Trump, about the war on Monday, with the two agreeing on the need to “continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life”. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion US envoys held talks in Kyiv on Sunday during an official visit to the country as part of an effort to end the conflict with Russia. While the talks were described as encouraging, no breakthrough was made. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said it appeared the war would continue into winter. https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.text: Polling by Refuge and End Violence Against Women found that one in five women had been stalked, monitored, harassed or controlled online. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Polling by Refuge and End Violence Against Women found that one in five women had been stalked, monitored, harassed or controlled online. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian Violence against women and girls Social platforms and police are failing women abused online, report finds Exclusive: Nearly half of survey respondents aged 16-24 have experienced violence on the internet, with many saying their complaints were not taken seriously Rachel Hall Tue 22 Sep 2026 11.27 EDT Last modified on Tue 22 Sep 2026 12.06 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google When Jane* learned that intimate photos of her had been posted on a website without her consent, she expected the police would help her. Instead, she was warned that researching where her photos had been shared might put her at risk of breaking the law. After she was handed a leaflet on internet safety and told to go to tech companies for help, but to expect little from them, the case was closed. “The officer called us at all times of day and approached the case in a way that was insensitive, victim-blaming and entirely inappropriate, with misogynistic undertones,” she recalled. Jane’s Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat accounts had all been hacked, along with those of several other women, and the images extracted from private messages. The incident was incredibly distressing: on the platform where the images were posted, commenters left derogatory messages, and one stranger used identifying personal data – including names of people and schools and links to social media profiles – to contact Jane directly. “I felt exposed, harassed, and stalked online by a community of anonymous perverts,” she said. “The experience left me feeling angry, violated and unsafe.” Like many women who have had similar experiences, Jane has moved more of her life offline and no longer feels comfortable in many online spaces. A new report from Refuge and End Violence Against Women (EVAW) says: “For many women, abuse, harassment and exposure to misogynistic content have become an ‘accepted risk’ of participating in online spaces.” It says this is despite Ofcom introducing voluntary guidance for tech companies on tackling violence against women and girls one year ago. View image in fullscreen Ofcom has launched voluntary guidance for tech companies on tackling violence against women and girls, but campaigners say it is not enough. Photograph: Kevin Foy/Alamy Disheartened by the traumatic reporting process, Jane appointed the law firm Leigh Day, which successfully pressed Ofcom into opening a formal investigation into the platforms , and the police into reopening their criminal investigation – though she feels there has been “little to no clarity or transparency” about how long these will take. Part of the difficulty when looking into such cases is that perpetrators can be based around the world and are able to conceal the IP addresses that identify their locations. But Jane argues this is no different from other online crime and no barrier to action, saying: “We wouldn’t expect the same response when it comes to other serious and complex crimes, such as terrorism.” Refuge and EVAW’s report found that most women in situations similar to Jane’s did not report their experiences to online platforms or the police, and when they did they often felt the response was poor. In many cases, they felt their complaints were misunderstood or not taken seriously, they were told to adapt their own behaviour, and either no action was taken or it was too slow. A survey of 2,000 women for the report found that 17% of those who made a complaint to the police did not have their cases investigated at all. It also found that nearly half (47%) of those surveyed aged 16-24 had experienced violence online, with one in four experiencing misogyny or sexual violence. One in five had been stalked, monitored, harassed or controlled; 18% had experienced image-based abuse, including being sent unsolicited images or having their intimate images shared without consent; and 9% had been doxed, meaning their personal information, such as phone numbers and addresses, was shared online. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Nearly one in three of women of all ages had been affected, and one in seven said they had left social media platforms as a result. For 15% of respondents, the level of abuse was so bad they said they had felt suicidal. The research also found that one in six women aged 16-24 had received dating, sex and relationships advice from an AI chatbot that they considered inappropriate, unhealthy or unsafe. Gemma Sherrington, the chief executive of Refuge, said that while Ofcom’s guidance was a welcome step, the regulator “must go much further in holding tech companies legally responsible for combating the normalisation of misogyny, holding perpetrators to account, and keeping all women and survivors safe”. The report also called for enhanced tech abuse training for police and prosecutors, a new online safety commission or ombuds role, ringfenced funding for the specialist services, and for Ofcom be empowered to take “swifter and more robust enforcement action”. An Ofcom spokesperson said: “Tackling the harms that women and girls disproportionately face online is a top priority for Ofcom. The law is clear that tech firms must take down illegal content – including harassment, stalking, violent threats and abuse – when they become aware of it. “We’re also cracking down on the spread of illegal intimate images, forcing tech firms to act to stop such content spreading on their platforms, as well as tightening our codes to reflect new quicker takedown timeframes. “We’ve also shown we won’t hesitate to act where tech firms fall short, with investigations open into three services for suspected failures to prevent individuals from encountering illegal intimate abuse imagery and other illegal content. We’re working to conclude these as swiftly as possible, following a fair, robust and transparent process.” *Name has been changed Explore more on these topics Violence against women and girls Online abuse Social media Ofcom Facebook Meta Instagram news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland
